subject: Am I misunderstanding the results from irace?

messages.author: 8d4cd0b2463d6bd3
messages.subject: Am I misunderstanding the results from irace?
parts: I have run irace on some problems and it outputted some top 6 configurations for my algorithm. But when I try my algorithm with the top 2 configurations, on all training instances, the configuration in 2nd position (irace) is actually better than the configuration in 1st position. Does irace not use all the training instances when comparing the final results or what is going on?

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] Am I misunderstanding the results from irace?
parts:
Hi Daniel,

Depending on the number of training instances and the budget available, irace
may use or not all training instances. You can see how many have been used by
looking at the highest number in the column "Instance" of the last iteration.

Also, how do you define better? Better mean or better in more instances?
Although the two are often correlated, by default, irace optimizes the latter.

Even if all instances are used, when the algorithms are stochastic, is the
difference between the two statistically significant? If the output has a large
variance (specially if it has outliers), it may also be chance that one is
better than the other in a single comparison. Maybe configuration #2 was
unlucky under irace or configuration #1 was unlucky when you ran it yourself.

Also, are you running the algorithms like irace is running them? That is, same
termination criteria, same computer, exactly the same parameter settings, etc.

Finally, the fact that irace printed those configurations at the end means that
irace could not discard any of them according to the Friedman test, so as far
as irace can tell they are statistically equivalent, although some may have a
better sum of ranks than the others in the particular runs that irace did.

The user-guide explains how to get all the data examined by irace, so it is
easy to check how irace made its decision and whether something needs to be
changed in the scenario setup.

Cheers,

Manuel.
